generatedProse.concept-context: In the School of Sport, where modules can cover a wide spread of theory, practical skills and clinical reasoning, having no revision plan is a fast route to anxiety. The material feels endless, and last-minute reading rarely sticks. A simple strategy, sharing your time across topics and finding where your understanding is thin, replaces that dread with manageable steps.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two sport therapy and rehabilitation students have the same exam in two weeks.

Tom has no plan. He tells himself there is time, then realises late how much there is to cover across assessment techniques, injury mechanisms and rehab protocols. The last few days are a rush of rereading, long into the night. He arrives exhausted and anxious, unsure what has gone in.

Amara makes a simple plan. She lists the topics, checks which techniques and protocols she cannot yet explain, and spreads her time across the two weeks, giving the weak spots more attention. She still feels nervous, but the nerves are manageable, because she knows she has covered the ground.

Both wanted to do well. Only Amara had a strategy, and it was the strategy that kept the anxiety in check.
generatedProse.summary: In the School of Sport, much exam anxiety grows from having no revision strategy, and a strategy is simply a plan for how you prepare. An effective plan rests on using your time well and finding the gaps in your understanding. You can now explain why a strategy matters, recognise how it eases anxiety, and name an early step towards one. That is the foundation the next sport courses build on.

check.body: In the worked example, what helped Amara feel calmer going into the exam?

items.text: She had a plan that used her time and targeted the techniques and protocols she could not yet explain.
She simply worried less and hoped for the best.
She left all her revision until the night before.
She decided the exam did not matter to her.

feedback.correct: That's right. A plan that used her time and targeted her gaps left Amara feeling prepared.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what Amara did that Tom did not.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara felt calmer because she had a strategy: it used her time and found her gaps. Hoping, cramming or not caring are not what helped.
